llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, cogito_3b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0496 (median 0) and satisfied just 40 % of the ≥75 % coverage threshold, indicating that most queries were answered with virtually no factual content. The dominant failure mode was the complete omission of tool usage, occurring in 232 cases (46.4 % of all tasks); this “no_tool_use” error directly caused every required claim to be missed. Secondary but still substantial problems were task misunderstanding (122 instances, 24.4 %) and early termination after a successful or partial tool call (96 instances, 19.2 %), showing that the model often either mis‑interprets the request or aborts before synthesising retrieved data. Tool calls were made in only 257 tasks (51.4 % of the sample), while the remaining 243 (48.6 %) relied solely on internal reasoning, yet even when tools were invoked the outputs were frequently discarded, leading to early‑termination failures. To remediate this, we recommend augmenting the training data and inference‑time prompting with explicit “must‑use‑tool” constraints and step‑by‑step scaffolding that forces the model to verify whether required external information is available before producing a final answer. What sets cogito_3b_output apart from other evaluated models is the unusually high proportion of pure cognitive attempts (nearly half of all runs) combined with a systematic inability to transition from tool acquisition to claim synthesis, rather than isolated hallucinations or API‑specific errors.
